name: Addison Disease

ethnicAssociations: All ethnicities; autoimmune form more common in European populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline for Primary Adrenal Insufficiency

criteria.description: Low morning serum cortisol (<3 mcg/dL strongly suggestive; 3-15 mcg/dL requires further testing)
Elevated ACTH (>2x upper limit of normal)
Subnormal cortisol response to ACTH stimulation test (peak cortisol <18 mcg/dL after 250 mcg cosyntropin)
Low serum aldosterone with elevated plasma renin activity (mineralocorticoid deficiency)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Biochemical confirmation: low cortisol (morning or stimulated) with elevated ACTH. 21-hydroxylase antibodies confirm autoimmune etiology.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Autoimmune adrenalitis is the most common cause in developed countries (~80%). Must exclude infectious (TB, HIV), infiltrative, hemorrhagic, and metastatic causes.

pathognomonic.notes: ACTH-driven melanocyte stimulation; affects skin creases, buccal mucosa, areolae, scars; distinguishes primary from secondary AI
Due to aldosterone deficiency and sodium wasting

occasional.symptomName: Loss of axillary and pubic hair (women)

rare.notes: Life-threatening; precipitated by stress, infection, surgery; shock, altered consciousness, severe hypotension

laboratory: Low morning cortisol (<3 mcg/dL diagnostic; 3-15 mcg/dL indeterminate)
Subnormal ACTH stimulation test (peak cortisol <18 mcg/dL)
Low aldosterone with elevated plasma renin activity
imaging: CT adrenal glands: small atrophic adrenals (autoimmune); enlarged/calcified (TB, hemorrhage, infiltrative)
genetic: AIRE gene mutations (in autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1)
other: Associated autoimmune conditions screen: thyroid function, vitamin B12, glucose/HbA1c, celiac antibodies, gonadal function

distinguishingFeatures: Often from chronic exogenous glucocorticoid use

redFlags: Adrenal crisis: severe hypotension, shock, acute abdomen, altered consciousness (emergency - IV hydrocortisone STAT)
Concurrent illness in known Addison patient without stress-dose steroids
Associated autoimmune conditions suggesting polyglandular syndrome
references: Bornstein SR, et al. Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016;101(2):364-389.
Husebye ES, et al. Adrenal insufficiency. Lancet. 2021;397(10274):613-629.

Betterle C, et al. Autoimmune adrenal insufficiency and autoimmune polyendocrine syndromes: autoantibodies, autoantigens, and their applicability in diagnosis and disease prediction. Endocr Rev. 2002;23(3):327-364.
